title: What belongs to grace freely given (1 Corinthians 12)
source_text: XIII. Itaque ad gratiam gratis datam pertinent sermo scientiae, sermo sapientiae, donum prophetiae, discretio spirituum, genera linguarum, operatio virtutum, gratia sanitatum, & plura ejusmodi quae Apostolus enumerat capite duodecimo prioris ad Corinthios, inter quae dona quaedam sunt, ex quibus beneficia corporalia consequuntur, ut bona valetudo, ex gratia sanitatum; sed quia praecipuus atque ultimus finis omnis gratiae gratis datae est salus animae sempiterna, idcirco omnem ejusmodi gratiam, ad aliorum salutem spiritualem conferri in superius allata definitione dictum est.
pass_a_gloss: XIII. And so to grace freely given pertain the word of knowledge, the word of wisdom, the gift of prophecy, discerning of spirits, kinds of tongues, working of powers, grace of healings, and more of this kind which the Apostle enumerates in the twelfth chapter of the first to the Corinthians, among which gifts certain ones are, from which bodily benefits follow, as good health, from the grace of healings; but because the chief and last end of all grace freely given is the everlasting salvation of the soul, therefore in the definition brought above it was said that all grace of this kind, is conferred for the spiritual salvation of others.
pass_b_english: Thesis XIII. Grace freely given therefore includes the word of knowledge, the word of wisdom, the gift of prophecy, the discerning of spirits, kinds of tongues, the working of miracles, the gift of healing, and the other gifts of this kind that the Apostle lists in 1 Corinthians 12.

Some of these gifts bring bodily benefits, as the gift of healing brings good health. But since the chief and final end of all grace freely given is the eternal salvation of the soul, the definition given above said that all such grace is conferred for the spiritual salvation of others.
